author.name: Laur\`ene Vaugrante, Anietta Weckauff, Thilo Hagendorff

entry.summary: Investigates emergent misalignment in LLMs fine-tuned on incorrect trivia, showing that emergently misaligned GPT-4.1 models demonstrate behavioral self-awareness of their misalignment state that shifts with subsequent realignment fine-tuning.

entry.title: Think Deep, Not Just Long: Measuring LLM Reasoning Effort via Deep-Thinking Tokens

author.name: Wei-Lin Chen, Liqian Peng, Tian Tan, Chao Zhao, Blake JianHang Chen, Ziqian Lin, Alec Go, Yu Meng

entry.summary: Proposes measuring LLM reasoning effort via 'deep-thinking tokens' where internal predictions undergo significant revisions in deeper model layers, rather than using raw token count. Tests across AIME, HMMT, and GPQA benchmarks on models including GPT-OSS and DeepSeek, showing this metric better predicts accuracy than chain length.

entry.title: Image Generation with a Sphere Encoder

author.name: Kaiyu Yue, Menglin Jia, Ji Hou, Tom Goldstein

entry.summary: Introduces the Sphere Encoder, a generative image framework that maps images onto a spherical latent space and generates images in a single forward pass, competing with multi-step diffusion models. The approach uses only reconstruction losses, supports conditional generation, and can improve quality with encoder/decoder looping.

entry.title: DM0: An Embodied-Native Vision-Language-Action Model towards Physical AI

author.name: En Yu, Haoran Lv, Jianjian Sun, Kangheng Lin, Ruitao Zhang, Yukang Shi, Yuyang Chen, Ze Chen, Ziheng Zhang, Fan Jia, Kaixin Liu, Meng Zhang, Ruitao Hao, Saike Huang, Songhan Xie, Yu Liu, Zhao Wu, Bin Xie, Pengwei Zhang, Qi Yang, Xianchi Deng, Yunfei Wei, Enwen Zhang, Hongyang Peng, Jie Zhao, Kai Liu, Wei Sun, Yajun Wei, Yi Yang, Yunqiao Zhang, Ziwei Yan, Haitao Yang, Hao Liu, Haoqiang Fan, Haowei Zhang, Junwen Huang, Yang Chen, Yunchao Ma, Yunhuan Yang, Zhengyuan Du, Ziming Liu, Jiahui Niu, Yucheng Zhao, Daxin Jiang, Wenbin Tang, Xiangyu Zhang, Zheng Ge, Erjin Zhou, Tiancai Wang

entry.summary: DM0 is an embodied-native VLA framework that unifies manipulation and navigation by learning from heterogeneous data sources from the onset, following a three-stage pipeline (Pretraining, Mid-Training, Post-Training) integrating web, driving, and embodied data.

entry.title: On Dwarkesh Patel’s 2026 Podcast With Dario Amodei

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi Mowshowitz's detailed commentary on Dario Amodei's 2026 podcast with Dwarkesh Patel. Key takeaways: Dario maintains predictions of extremely rapid AI capability growth (possibly 'geniuses in a data center' this year), downplays catastrophic risk relative to past statements, and notably there was almost no discussion of alignment — 'the dog did not bark.'

entry.title: Attention in Constant Time: Vashista Sparse Attention for Long-Context Decoding with Exponential Guarantees

author.name: Vashista Nobaub

entry.summary: Formalizes attention as projection onto convex hulls of key vectors and proves a face-stability theorem showing attention concentrates on a constant-size active face under strict complementarity, enabling constant-time sparse attention with exponential guarantees.

entry.title: Boule or Baguette? A Study on Task Topology, Length Generalization, and the Benefit of Reasoning Traces

author.name: William L. Tong, Ege Cakar, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: Introduces PITA, a 23M+ statement dataset in propositional logic for studying length generalization in reasoning models. Proposes task depth and task breadth as dimensions explaining when reasoning traces help and when models fail to generalize.

entry.title: Evolutionary System Prompt Learning can Facilitate Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

author.name: Lunjun Zhang, Ryan Chen, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Proposes Evolutionary System Prompt Learning (E-SPL), jointly optimizing LLM contexts (system prompts) and weights through evolutionary algorithms combined with RL. Uses TrueSkill ratings for prompt selection with mutation/crossover operations.

entry.title: BitDance: Scaling Autoregressive Generative Models with Binary Tokens

author.name: Yuang Ai, Jiaming Han, Shaobin Zhuang, Weijia Mao, Xuefeng Hu, Ziyan Yang, Zhenheng Yang, Huaibo Huang, Xiangyu Yue, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Presents BitDance, an autoregressive image generator using binary visual tokens where each token can represent up to 2^256 states, with a binary diffusion head for sampling and next-patch parallel decoding for faster inference.

entry.title: HLE-Verified: A Systematic Verification and Structured Revision of Humanity's Last Exam

author.name: Weiqi Zhai, Zhihai Wang, Jinghang Wang, Boyu Yang, Xiaogang Li, Xiang Xu, Bohan Wang, Peng Wang, Xingzhe Wu, Anfeng Li, Qiyuan Feng, Yuhao Zhou, Shoulin Han, Wenjie Luo, Yiyuan Li, Yaxuan Wang, Ruixian Luo, Guojie Lin, Peiyao Xiao, Chengliang Xu, Ben Wang, Zeyu Wang, Zichao Chen, Jianan Ye, Yijie Hu, Jialong Chen, Zongwen Shen, Yuliang Xu, An Yang, Bowen Yu, Dayiheng Liu, Junyang Lin, Hu Wei, Que Shen, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces HLE-Verified, a cleaned and verified version of Humanity's Last Exam benchmark with a transparent verification protocol and error taxonomy. Found that existing HLE contains noisy items that bias evaluation and distort cross-model comparisons.

entry.title: RynnBrain: Open Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Ronghao Dang, Jiayan Guo, Bohan Hou, Sicong Leng, Kehan Li, Xin Li, Jiangpin Liu, Yunxuan Mao, Zhikai Wang, Yuqian Yuan, Minghao Zhu, Xiao Lin, Yang Bai, Qian Jiang, Yaxi Zhao, Minghua Zeng, Junlong Gao, Yuming Jiang, Jun Cen, Siteng Huang, Liuyi Wang, Wenqiao Zhang, Chengju Liu, Jianfei Yang, Shijian Lu, Deli Zhao

entry.summary: RynnBrain is an open-source spatiotemporal foundation model for embodied intelligence with three scales (2B, 8B, 30B-A3B MoE) and four post-trained variants, strengthening egocentric understanding, spatiotemporal localization, physical reasoning, and physics-aware planning.

entry.title: Information Fidelity in Tool-Using LLM Agents: A Martingale Analysis of the Model Context Protocol

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Roger Wattenhofer, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical framework for error accumulation in Model Context Protocol (MCP) agents, proving linear growth of cumulative distortion with O(√T) concentration bounds via martingale analysis. Rules out exponential failure modes.

entry.title: CORPGEN: Simulating Corporate Environments with Autonomous Digital Employees in Multi-Horizon Task Environments

author.name: Abubakarr Jaye, Nigel Boachie Kumankumah, Chidera Biringa, Anjel Shaileshbhai Patel, Sulaiman Vesal, Dayquan Julienne, Charlotte Siska, Manuel Ra\'ul Mel\'endez Luj\'an, Anthony Twum-Barimah, Mauricio Velazco, Tianwei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Horizon Task Environments (MHTEs) for evaluating autonomous agents on concurrent long-horizon tasks with interleaving and dependencies. Identifies four failure modes causing baseline agents to degrade from 16.7% to 8.7% completion as load scales.

entry.title: Diagnosing Knowledge Conflict in Multimodal Long-Chain Reasoning

author.name: Jing Tang, Kun Wang, Haolang Lu, Hongjin Chen, KaiTao Chen, Zhongxiang Sun, Qiankun Li, Lingjuan Lyu, Guoshun Nan, Zhigang Zeng

entry.summary: Formalizes knowledge conflict in multimodal LLMs during long chain-of-thought reasoning, showing different conflict types are linearly separable in model representations, concentrate in mid-to-late layers, and follow hierarchical consistency patterns.

entry.title: MoltNet: Understanding Social Behavior of AI Agents in the Agent-Native MoltBook

author.name: Yi Feng, Chen Huang, Zhibo Man, Ryner Tan, Long P. Hoang, Shaoyang Xu, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents MoltNet, a large-scale empirical analysis of AI agent social behavior on MoltBook, a social networking platform for AI agents, examining emergent social dynamics across four sociological dimensions using data from early 2026.

entry.title: Finding Highly Interpretable Prompt-Specific Circuits in Language Models

author.name: Gabriel Franco, Lucas M. Tassis, Azalea Rohr, Mark Crovella

entry.summary: Introduces ACC++, a method for extracting prompt-specific circuits in language models that challenges the assumption of single stable mechanisms per task. Shows circuits are prompt-specific even within a fixed task, without requiring activation patching.

entry.title: You Can Learn Tokenization End-to-End with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sam Dauncey, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Shows that tokenization boundaries can be learned end-to-end using reinforcement learning (score function estimates) rather than heuristics or straight-through estimators, directly optimizing the discrete boundary selection problem.

entry.title: A Rational Analysis of the Effects of Sycophantic AI

author.name: Rafael M. Batista, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Provides a Bayesian rational analysis showing that sycophantic AI (overly agreeable LLMs) creates a unique epistemic risk by reinforcing existing beliefs, distinct from hallucinations. Demonstrates through mathematical framework and experiments.

entry.title: Broken Chains: The Cost of Incomplete Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Ian Su, Gaurav Purushothaman, Jey Narayan, Ruhika Goel, Kevin Zhu, Sunishchal Dev, Yash More, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: Introduces a framework constraining reasoning models to use code, natural language, hybrid, or no reasoning under token budget limits, evaluating GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Flash, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Grok 4.1 on math benchmarks. Finds truncated reasoning can hurt more than no reasoning, and models vary in robustness to budget constraints.

entry.title: Efficient Sampling with Discrete Diffusion Models: Sharp and Adaptive Guarantees

author.name: Daniil Dmitriev, Zhihan Huang, Yuting Wei

entry.summary: Establishes sharp convergence guarantees for discrete diffusion model sampling under continuous-time Markov chain formulation, achieving O(d/ε) iteration complexity for uniform discrete diffusion that eliminates dependence on vocabulary size. Provides the first polynomial complexity bounds for masked discrete diffusion.

entry.title: Overthinking Loops in Agents: A Structural Risk via MCP Tools

author.name: Yohan Lee, Jisoo Jang, Seoyeon Choi, Sangyeop Kim, Seungtaek Choi

entry.summary: Demonstrates that malicious MCP tool servers can induce overthinking loops in LLM agents through structural attacks that create cyclic tool-calling trajectories inflating tokens and latency without any single step appearing abnormal. Tests 14 malicious tools across three servers.

entry.title: Diagnosing Pathological Chain-of-Thought in Reasoning Models

author.name: Manqing Liu, David Williams-King, Ida Caspary, Linh Le, Hannes Whittingham, Puria Radmard, Cameron Tice, Edward James Young

entry.summary: Creates concrete metrics and methods to diagnose three pathological CoT behaviors: post-hoc rationalization, encoded reasoning (concealing information in text), and internalized reasoning (replacing explicit steps with filler). Critical for CoT monitoring and safety.

entry.title: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yiran Peng, Yiyu Chen, Jianhao Ruan, Zijie Zhuang, Cheng Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Man Chen, Yenchi Tseng, Zhaoyang Yu, Liang Chen, Yuyao Zhai, Bang Liu, Chenglin Wu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: Proposes AutoWebWorld, a framework for synthesizing verifiable web environments by modeling them as Finite State Machines, enabling controllable training data generation for web agents. Uses coding agents to translate FSMs into interactive websites.

entry.title: AISA: Awakening Intrinsic Safety Awareness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Weiming Song, Xuan Xie, Ruiping Yin

entry.summary: Presents AISA, a lightweight single-pass defense against jailbreak attacks that activates latent safety behaviors inside the model by localizing intrinsic safety awareness via spatiotemporal analysis of attention heads.

entry.title: BFS-PO: Best-First Search for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Fiorenzo Parascandolo, Wenhui Tan, Enver Sangineto, Ruihua Song, Rita Cucchiara

entry.summary: Proposes BFS-PO, an RL algorithm using best-first search with backtracking via maximum entropy nodes to find shorter correct reasoning chains, addressing overthinking in large reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1.

entry.title: On Calibration of Large Language Models: From Response To Capability

author.name: Sin-Han Yang, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Hung-yi Lee, Shao-Hua Sun

entry.summary: Introduces capability calibration for LLMs, which targets expected accuracy on a query rather than single-response correctness. Shows response-level calibration is misaligned with practical needs due to stochastic decoding.

entry.title: A Geometric Taxonomy of Hallucinations in LLMs

author.name: Javier Mar\'in

entry.summary: Proposes a geometric taxonomy of LLM hallucinations (unfaithfulness, confabulation, factual error) based on embedding space signatures. Finds domain-local detection works well (AUROC 0.76-0.99) but cross-domain detection fails (AUROC 0.50), with human-crafted confabulations being geometrically distinct.

entry.title: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage

author.name: Akshat Naik, Jay Culligan, Yarin Gal, Philip Torr, Rahaf Aljundi, Alasdair Paren, Adel Bibi

entry.summary: OMNI-LEAK demonstrates a novel data leakage attack in multi-agent orchestrator systems where a compromised specialist agent can extract data from other agents despite access controls. Highlights security vulnerabilities in the popular orchestrator pattern.

entry.title: Ambient Physics: Training Neural PDE Solvers with Partial Observations

author.name: Harris Abdul Majid, Giannis Daras, Francesco Tudisco, Steven McDonagh

entry.summary: Ambient Physics learns joint distributions of PDE coefficient-solution pairs from partial observations only, using random masking of observed measurements so the model cannot distinguish truly vs artificially unobserved data.

entry.title: Precedent-Informed Reasoning: Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Models via Test-Time Precedent Learning

author.name: Qianyue Wang, Jinwu Hu, Huanxiang Lin, Bolin Chen, Zhiquan Wen, Yaofo Chen, Yu Rong, Mingkui Tan

entry.summary: Proposes Precedent Informed Reasoning (PIR) to address overthinking in large reasoning models by retrieving and leveraging past solved problems to guide new reasoning, reducing redundant self-exploration at test time.

entry.title: Computability of Agentic Systems

author.name: Chatavut Viriyasuthee

entry.summary: Introduces Quest Graph, a formal framework analyzing computational power of agentic systems with finite context. Shows forward-only finite quest decision processes are equivalent to pushdown automata while reference-augmented versions can regain Turing completeness.

entry.title: Preventing Rank Collapse in Federated Low-Rank Adaptation with Client Heterogeneity

author.name: Fei Wu, Jia Hu, Geyong Min, Shiqiang Wang

entry.summary: Identifies 'rank collapse' in heterogeneous federated LoRA, where global update energy concentrates on the minimum shared rank. Provides theoretical analysis of the root cause and proposes solutions.

entry.title: Singular Vectors of Attention Heads Align with Features

author.name: Gabriel Franco, Carson Loughridge, Mark Crovella

entry.summary: Demonstrates that singular vectors of attention heads in language models robustly align with features, providing theoretical justification under various conditions. Proposes operational methods to recognize alignment in real models.

entry.title: Mitigating the Safety-utility Trade-off in LLM Alignment via Adaptive Safe Context Learning

author.name: Yanbo Wang, Minzheng Wang, Jian Liang, Lu Wang, Yongcan Yu, Ran He

entry.summary: Proposes ASCL, a framework for mitigating the safety-utility trade-off in reasoning model alignment by formulating safety as a multi-turn tool-use process rather than rigid rule memorization through context distillation.

entry.title: WoVR: World Models as Reliable Simulators for Post-Training VLA Policies with RL

author.name: Zhennan Jiang, Shangqing Zhou, Yutong Jiang, Zefang Huang, Mingjie Wei, Yuhui Chen, Tianxing Zhou, Zhen Guo, Hao Lin, Quanlu Zhang, Yu Wang, Haoran Li, Chao Yu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes WoVR, a framework using world models as simulators for RL-based post-training of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies, addressing hallucination and error accumulation in imagined rollouts with reliability-aware mechanisms.

entry.title: SkillJect: Automating Stealthy Skill-Based Prompt Injection for Coding Agents with Trace-Driven Closed-Loop Refinement

author.name: Xiaojun Jia, Jie Liao, Simeng Qin, Jindong Gu, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao, Yang Liu, Philip Torr

entry.summary: Introduces SkillJect, the first automated framework for stealthy prompt injection attacks targeting coding agent skills, using a closed-loop Attack-Judge-Defense agent system to synthesize hard-to-detect poisoned skills.

entry.title: Unlocking Reasoning Capability on Machine Translation in Large Language Models

author.name: Sara Rajaee, Sebastian Vincent, Alexandre Berard, Marzieh Fadaee, Kelly Marchisio, Tom Kocmi

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates reasoning LLMs on machine translation and finds that explicit reasoning consistently degrades translation quality. MT reasoning traces are linear, lacking self-correction. Proposes training approaches to unlock reasoning for MT.

entry.title: Rethinking Diffusion Models with Symmetries through Canonicalization with Applications to Molecular Graph Generation

author.name: Cai Zhou, Zijie Chen, Zian Li, Jike Wang, Kaiyi Jiang, Pan Li, Rose Yu, Muhan Zhang, Stephen Bates, Tommi Jaakkola

entry.summary: Challenges the standard approach of enforcing equivariance through architecture by proposing canonicalization: mapping samples to orbit representatives, training unconstrained models on canonical forms, then recovering invariance via random symmetry transforms. Provides comprehensive theory and applies to molecular generation.

entry.title: Divine Benevolence is an $x^2$: GLUs scale asymptotically faster than MLPs

author.name: Alejandro Francisco Queiruga

entry.summary: Provides a numerical analysis explanation for why GLU architectures scale better than MLPs: GLUs have piecewise quadratic forms enabling L(P)∝P^{-3} scaling vs P^{-2} for MLPs. Explains the empirical success of GLUs in frontier LLMs from first principles.

entry.title: Small Reward Models via Backward Inference

author.name: Yike Wang, Faeze Brahman, Shangbin Feng, Teng Xiao, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: Proposes FLIP, a reward modeling approach that works by backward inference - inferring the instruction that would produce a given response and using similarity to the original instruction as the reward signal. This is reference-free and rubric-free, enabling smaller models to serve as effective reward models.

entry.title: Estimating METR Time Horizons for Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.3 Codex (xhigh)

author.name: CharlesD

entry.summary: Provides independent analysis and estimation of METR time horizons for Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.3-Codex, two of the most recent frontier models. Critically examines how METR benchmarks are constructed and cautions about sensitivity of time horizon estimates to task selection and methodology.

entry.title: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web

author.name: Jaechul Roh, Eugene Bagdasarian, Hamed Haddadi, Ali Shahin Shamsabadi

entry.summary: SPILLage formalizes 'Natural Agentic Oversharing' - unintentional disclosure of task-irrelevant user information by web agents during task execution. Characterizes oversharing along channel (content vs. behavior) and direction dimensions.

entry.title: Statistical Early Stopping for Reasoning Models

author.name: Yangxinyu Xie, Tao Wang, Soham Mallick, Yan Sun, Georgy Noarov, Mengxin Yu, Tanwi Mallick, Weijie J. Su, Edgar Dobriban

entry.summary: Introduces statistically principled early stopping for reasoning models that monitors uncertainty signals during generation. Includes parametric (renewal process) and nonparametric approaches with finite-sample guarantees against premature stopping.

entry.title: Backdooring Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Anudeep Das, Prach Chantasantitam, Gurjot Singh, Lipeng He, Mariia Ponomarenko, Florian Kerschbaum

entry.summary: Studies backdoor attacks that induce bias in LLMs through a white-box threat model where the model builder is the adversary. Focuses on semantically-triggered attacks for bias manipulation, going beyond prior syntactic trigger approaches.

entry.title: Train Less, Learn More: Adaptive Efficient Rollout Optimization for Group-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhi Zhang, Zhen Han, Costas Mavromatis, Qi Zhu, Yunyi Zhang, Sheng Guan, Dingmin Wang, Xiong Zhou, Shuai Wang, Soji Adeshina, Vassilis Ioannidis, Huzefa Rangwala

entry.summary: Introduces AERO, an enhancement to GRPO for LLM RL that uses adaptive rollout strategy, selective rejection of uninformative groups, and Bayesian posterior for efficient rollout allocation.

entry.title: On-Policy Supervised Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Anhao Zhao, Ziyang Chen, Junlong Tong, Yingqi Fan, Fanghua Ye, Shuhao Li, Yunpu Ma, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Shows that on-policy supervised fine-tuning can match RL-based reasoning training by removing KL regularization and group-wise normalization, simplifying the training pipeline while maintaining strong reasoning performance.

entry.title: OneLatent: Single-Token Compression for Visual Latent Reasoning

author.name: Bo Lv, Yasheng Sun, Junjie Wang, Haoxiang Shi

entry.summary: OneLatent compresses chain-of-thought reasoning into a single latent token supervised by rendered CoT images and DeepSeek-OCR hidden states, reducing output length by 11x with only 2.21% accuracy drop.

entry.title: G2CP: A Graph-Grounded Communication Protocol for Verifiable and Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Karim Ben Khaled, Davy Monticolo

entry.summary: Proposes G2CP, a graph-grounded communication protocol for multi-agent systems where agents communicate via graph operations over a shared knowledge graph rather than free text, reducing semantic drift and hallucination propagation.

entry.title: Deep Dense Exploration for LLM Reinforcement Learning via Pivot-Driven Resampling

author.name: Yiran Guo, Zhongjian Qiao, Yingqi Xie, Jie Liu, Dan Ye, Ruiqing Zhang, Shuang Qiu, Lijie Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Deep Dense Exploration (DDE) for LLM RL, focusing sampling budget on 'pivots' - recoverable states within unsuccessful trajectories - rather than sampling only from the root (GRPO) or blindly dispersing across states.

entry.title: Goldilocks RL: Tuning Task Difficulty to Escape Sparse Rewards for Reasoning

author.name: Ilia Mahrooghi, Aryo Lotfi, Emmanuel Abbe

entry.summary: Proposes Goldilocks, a teacher-driven data sampling strategy for RL-based reasoning that predicts question difficulty and selects neither-too-easy-nor-too-hard questions for training, addressing sparse reward inefficiency.

entry.title: When to Think Fast and Slow? AMOR: Entropy-Based Metacognitive Gate for Dynamic SSM-Attention Switching

author.name: Haoran Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes AMOR, a hybrid architecture combining SSMs with sparse attention, dynamically switching based on prediction entropy inspired by dual-process cognition theory. Uses 'Ghost KV' to project keys/values from SSM hidden states, reusing O(n) computation.

entry.title: DPBench: Large Language Models Struggle with Simultaneous Coordination

author.name: Najmul Hasan, Prashanth BusiReddyGari

entry.summary: DPBench tests LLM coordination using the Dining Philosophers problem, revealing that GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5, and Grok 4.1 coordinate well sequentially but fail catastrophically (>95% deadlock) in simultaneous decision settings due to convergent reasoning.

entry.title: Text Before Vision: Staged Knowledge Injection Matters for Agentic RLVR in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Understanding

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Mingshuo Chen, Yueying Li, Yajie Yang, Yuhao Zhou, Di Wang, Yifan Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Haiyan Zhao, Hongda Sun, Long Lan, Jun Song, Yulin Wang, Jing Zhang, Wenlong Zhang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Investigates how text-only Earth-science QA surprisingly drives ultra-high-resolution remote sensing understanding better than visual training alone. Shows staged knowledge injection (text before vision) is critical for agentic RLVR in remote sensing.

entry.title: VisPhyWorld: Probing Physical Reasoning via Code-Driven Video Reconstruction

author.name: Jiarong Liang, Max Ku, Ka-Hei Hui, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes VisPhyWorld, an execution-based framework evaluating physical reasoning by requiring MLLMs to generate executable simulator code from visual observations, introducing VisPhyBench for evaluation.

entry.title: Visual Para-Thinker: Divide-and-Conquer Reasoning for Visual Comprehension

author.name: Haoran Xu, Hongyu Wang, Jiaze Li, Shunpeng Chen, Zizhao Tong, Jianzhong Ju, Zhenbo Luo, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Proposes Visual Para-Thinker, a parallel reasoning framework for multimodal LLMs that shifts from depth-based to parallelism-based test-time scaling by leveraging visual partitioning strategies. This addresses the exploration plateau problem in vertical scaling of reasoning chains.

entry.title: CellMaster: Collaborative Cell Type Annotation in Single-Cell Analysis

author.name: Zhen Wang, Yiming Gao, Jieyuan Liu, Enze Ma, Jefferson Chen, Mark Antkowiak, Mengzhou Hu, JungHo Kong, Dexter Pratt, Zhiting Hu, Wei Wang, Trey Ideker, Eric P. Xing

entry.summary: Presents CellMaster, an AI agent using LLM-encoded knowledge for zero-shot cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA-seq data without pre-training or fixed marker databases. Achieves 7.1% accuracy improvement over baselines across 9 datasets spanning 8 tissues.

entry.title: TrasMuon: Trust-Region Adaptive Scaling for Orthogonalized Momentum Optimizers

author.name: Peng Cheng, Jiucheng Zang, Qingnan Li, Liheng Ma, Yufei Cui, Yingxue Zhang, Boxing Chen, Ming Jian, Wen Tong

entry.summary: Introduces TrasMuon, an optimizer that adds trust-region adaptive scaling to Muon-style orthogonalized momentum optimizers, combining global RMS calibration with energy-based trust-region clipping to stabilize training.

entry.title: What happens when reviewers receive AI feedback in their reviews?

author.name: Shiping Chen, Shu Zhong, Duncan P. Brumby, Anna L. Cox

entry.summary: First empirical study of AI feedback tools deployed in a live peer review process (ICLR 2025), examining how reviewers engaged with AI-generated post-review suggestions through surveys and interviews. Provides unique evidence on opportunities and tensions when AI augments peer review.

entry.title: GSRM: Generative Speech Reward Model for Speech RLHF

author.name: Maohao Shen, Tejas Jayashankar, Osama Hanna, Naoyuki Kanda, Yancheng Wang, Kate\v{r}ina \v{Z}mol\'ikov\'a, Ruiming Xie, Niko Moritz, Anfeng Xu, Yashesh Gaur, Gregory Wornell, Qing He, Jilong Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Generative Speech Reward Model (GSRM), a reasoning-centric reward model for evaluating speech naturalness that decomposes evaluation into interpretable components rather than simple scalar scores. Designed for RLHF in speech language models like GPT-4o Voice Mode.

entry.title: Towards Spatial Transcriptomics-driven Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Konstantin Hemker, Andrew H. Song, Cristina Almagro-P\'erez, Guillaume Jaume, Sophia J. Wagner, Anurag Vaidya, Nikola Simidjievski, Mateja Jamnik, Faisal Mahmood

entry.summary: Introduces SEAL, a vision-omics self-supervised learning framework that infuses spatial transcriptomics molecular information into pathology vision encoders, improving histological representations. From Mahmood Lab at Harvard/BWH.

entry.title: Differentially Private Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Tingting Tang, James Flemings, Yongqin Wang, Murali Annavaram

entry.summary: Proposes differentially private RAG that integrates formal DP guarantees into retrieval-augmented generation, addressing privacy risks when databases contain sensitive documents like medical records.

entry.title: S2D: Selective Spectral Decay for Quantization-Friendly Conditioning of Neural Activations

author.name: Arnav Chavan, Nahush Lele, Udbhav Bamba, Sankalp Dayal, Aditi Raghunathan, Deepak Gupta

entry.summary: Identifies that activation outliers in large transformers (which hurt quantization) are directly linked to dominant singular values of weights, and proposes Selective Spectral Decay (S²D) to regularize only those components. Shows the problem worsens with pre-training scale (CLIP → SigLIP → SigLIP2). Practical method for making large vision models more quantization-friendly.

entry.title: Governing AI Forgetting: Auditing for Machine Unlearning Compliance

author.name: Qinqi Lin, Ningning Ding, Lingjie Duan, Jianwei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces the first economic framework for auditing machine unlearning compliance, integrating certified unlearning theory with regulatory enforcement through game-theoretic modeling of auditor-operator interactions and hypothesis testing.

entry.title: Residual Connections and the Causal Shift: Uncovering a Structural Misalignment in Transformers

author.name: Jonathan Lys, Vincent Gripon, Bastien Pasdeloup, Lukas Mauch, Fabien Cardinaux, Ghouthi Boukli Hacene

entry.summary: Identifies a structural misalignment in transformers where residual connections tie activations to current tokens while supervision targets next tokens, and proposes shifted residual connections to address this causal shift.

entry.title: Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows

author.name: Bardia Mohammadi, Nearchos Potamitis, Lars Klein, Akhil Arora, Laurent Bindschaedler

entry.summary: Introduces Atomix, a runtime providing transactional semantics for LLM agent tool calls with epoch-tracking, frontier-gated commit, and compensation on abort, preventing unintended side effects during failures or speculation.

entry.title: Long Context, Less Focus: A Scaling Gap in LLMs Revealed through Privacy and Personalization

author.name: Shangding Gu

entry.summary: Introduces PAPerBench (~29K instances, 377K evaluation questions, 1K-256K token contexts) showing that increasing context length degrades both privacy protection and personalization quality in LLMs, revealing a scaling gap.

entry.title: Attention Head Entropy of LLMs Predicts Answer Correctness

author.name: Sophie Ostmeier, Brian Axelrod, Maya Varma, Asad Aali, Yabin Zhang, Magdalini Paschali, Sanmi Koyejo, Curtis Langlotz, Akshay Chaudhari

entry.summary: Introduces Head Entropy, a method that predicts LLM answer correctness from attention entropy patterns using sparse logistic regression on per-head Rényi entropies. Shows this white-box approach matches or exceeds baselines and generalizes across domains.

entry.title: AsyncVLA: An Asynchronous VLA for Fast and Robust Navigation on the Edge

author.name: Noriaki Hirose, Catherine Glossop, Dhruv Shah, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Proposes AsyncVLA, an asynchronous control framework that decouples semantic reasoning (large VLA on remote workstation) from reactive execution (lightweight edge adapter) for real-time robot navigation. Demonstrates 2x improvement in success rate in dynamic environments.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for LLM Fine-tuning Using Early Stopping for Non-random Initialization

author.name: Zexuan Sun, Garvesh Raskutti

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework for LLM fine-tuning with early stopping by extending NTK theory to non-random (pretrained) initializations for attention-based models. Provides convergence guarantees explaining why few epochs suffice.

entry.title: A generalizable foundation model for intraoperative understanding across surgical procedures

author.name: Kanggil Park, Yongjun Jeon, Soyoung Lim, Seonmin Park, Jongmin Shin, Jung Yong Kim, Sehyeon An, Jinsoo Rhu, Jongman Kim, Gyu-Seong Choi, Namkee Oh, Kyu-Hwan Jung

entry.summary: Introduces ZEN, a foundation model for intraoperative surgical video understanding trained on 4M+ frames from 21+ procedures using self-supervised multi-teacher distillation. Demonstrates generalization across procedures and institutions.

entry.title: LaViDa-R1: Advancing Reasoning for Unified Multimodal Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Shufan Li, Yuchen Zhu, Jiuxiang Gu, Kangning Liu, Zhe Lin, Yongxin Chen, Molei Tao, Aditya Grover, Jason Kuen

entry.summary: Proposes LaViDa-R1, a multimodal reasoning diffusion language model that unifies understanding and generation tasks with a novel post-training framework combining SFT and multi-task RL with techniques like answer-forcing and tree search.

entry.title: TactAlign: Human-to-Robot Policy Transfer via Tactile Alignment

author.name: Youngsun Wi, Jessica Yin, Elvis Xiang, Akash Sharma, Jitendra Malik, Mustafa Mukadam, Nima Fazeli, Tess Hellebrekers

entry.summary: TactAlign transfers human-collected tactile signals from wearable gloves to robots with different embodiments, without requiring identical sensors or paired data. It transforms human tactile representations into robot-compatible signals for policy learning.

entry.title: Online LLM watermark detection via e-processes

author.name: Weijie Su, Ruodu Wang, Zinan Zhao

entry.summary: Develops a unified framework for LLM watermark detection using e-processes, providing anytime-valid guarantees for online testing. Proposes adaptive e-process construction methods and establishes theoretical power characterization.

entry.title: Jailbreaking is Empirical Evidence for Inner Misalignment and Against Alignment by Default

author.name: Jérémy Andréoletti

entry.summary: Argues that the persistent success of jailbreaking across LLM generations constitutes empirical evidence for inner misalignment — models trained on safety objectives develop surface-level compliance that breaks under distribution shift. This directly challenges the 'alignment by default' thesis that sufficient capability plus human-values-in-training-data yields aligned systems.

entry.title: Scaling the Scaling Logic: Agentic Meta-Synthesis of Logic Reasoning

author.name: Bowen Liu, Zhi Wu, Runquan Xie, Zhanhui Kang, Jia Li

entry.summary: SSLogic is an agentic meta-synthesis framework that scales verifiable training signals for RLVR by iteratively synthesizing Generator-Validator program pairs for logical reasoning tasks. Operates at the task-family level rather than instance-level perturbations.

entry.title: The Quantization Trap: Breaking Linear Scaling Laws in Multi-Hop Reasoning

author.name: Henry Han, Xiyang Liu, Xiaodong Wang, Fei Han, Xiaodong Li

entry.summary: Reveals a 'quantization trap' where reducing precision from 16-bit to 8/4-bit paradoxically increases energy consumption in multi-hop reasoning due to hardware casting overhead and dequantization kernel latency becoming dominant bottlenecks.

entry.title: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training

author.name: Yuan Cao, Dezhi Ran, Mengzhou Wu, Yuzhe Guo, Xin Chen, Ang Li, Gang Cao, Gong Zhi, Hao Yu, Linyi Li, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: GUI-GENESIS automatically synthesizes lightweight web GUI training environments with verifiable code-native rewards for agent post-training, addressing latency, reproducibility, and reward verification issues of real-world app training.

entry.title: REDSearcher: A Scalable and Cost-Efficient Framework for Long-Horizon Search Agents

author.name: Zheng Chu, Xiao Wang, Jack Hong, Huiming Fan, Yuqi Huang, Yue Yang, Guohai Xu, Chenxiao Zhao, Cheng Xiang, Shengchao Hu, Dongdong Kuang, Ming Liu, Bing Qin, Xing Yu

entry.summary: Proposes REDSearcher, a framework co-designing complex task synthesis, mid-training, and post-training for scalable search agent optimization. Addresses the sparsity of high-quality search trajectories through dual-constrained task synthesis optimization.

entry.title: Spectral Collapse in Diffusion Inversion

author.name: Nicolas Bourriez, Alexandre Verine, Auguste Genovesio

entry.summary: Identifies and characterizes 'spectral collapse' in diffusion model inversion, where deterministic inversion fails when source domain is spectrally sparse compared to target, leading to oversmoothed generations.

entry.title: AdaCorrection: Adaptive Offset Cache Correction for Accurate Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Dong Liu, Yanxuan Yu, Ben Lengerich, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: Introduces AdaCorrection, an adaptive cache correction framework for diffusion transformers that estimates cache validity with lightweight spatio-temporal signals, enabling efficient feature reuse while maintaining generation quality.

entry.title: Language Model Memory and Memory Models for Language

author.name: Benjamin L. Badger

entry.summary: Investigates language model memory by showing that standard LM embeddings contain relatively little input information regardless of scale, while autoencoder embeddings achieve near-perfect memory. Proposes a parallelizable encoder-decoder memory model architecture.

entry.title: Elo-Evolve: A Co-evolutionary Framework for Language Model Alignment

author.name: Jing Zhao, Ting Zhen, Junwei bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang song

entry.summary: Introduces Elo-Evolve, a co-evolutionary alignment framework that uses dynamic multi-agent competition instead of static reward models, learning from binary win/loss outcomes with Elo-orchestrated opponent selection.

entry.title: OmniScience: A Large-scale Multi-modal Dataset for Scientific Image Understanding

author.name: Haoyi Tao, Chaozheng Huang, Nan Wang, Han Lyu, Linfeng Zhang, Guolin Ke, Xi Fang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniScience, a large-scale multimodal dataset of 1.5M figure-caption-context triplets spanning 10+ scientific disciplines for training and evaluating scientific image understanding in MLLMs.

entry.title: Experiential Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Taiwei Shi, Sihao Chen, Bowen Jiang, Linxin Song, Longqi Yang, Jieyu Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces Experiential Reinforcement Learning (ERL), embedding an experience-reflection-consolidation loop into RL for LLMs, where models reflect on failures to guide refined attempts before reinforcing successful behaviors.

entry.title: DenseMLLM: Standard Multimodal LLMs are Intrinsic Dense Predictors

author.name: Yi Li, Hongze Shen, Lexiang Tang, Xin Li, Xinpeng Ding, Yinsong Liu, Deqiang Jiang, Xing Sun, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: Shows standard multimodal LLMs can perform dense predictions (segmentation, depth estimation) without task-specific decoders through a novel vision encoding strategy, challenging the need for complex architectural additions.

entry.title: SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data

author.name: David Chanin, Adri\`a Garriga-Alonso

entry.summary: Introduces SynthSAEBench, a toolkit for generating large-scale synthetic data with realistic feature characteristics to benchmark Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), including correlation, hierarchy, and superposition. Reproduces known LLM SAE phenomena.

entry.title: Why is Normalization Preferred? A Worst-Case Complexity Theory for Stochastically Preconditioned SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Yuchen Fang, James Demmel, Javad Lavaei

entry.summary: Develops worst-case complexity theory for stochastically preconditioned SGD (covering Adam, RMSProp, Shampoo) under heavy-tailed noise, showing a fundamental separation between normalization and clipping approaches.

entry.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift

author.name: Max Fomin

entry.summary: Analyzes malicious prompt classifiers using Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) evaluation, revealing that standard train-test splits from same dataset sources severely overestimate out-of-distribution performance for jailbreak/injection detection.

entry.title: High-accuracy log-concave sampling with stochastic queries

author.name: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Constantinos Daskalakis, Alexander Rakhlin

entry.summary: Proves that high-accuracy log-concave sampling (polylog(1/δ) complexity) is achievable with stochastic gradients having subexponential tails, establishing a separation from convex optimization. Shows light tails are necessary.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating Post-hoc Rationalization in Reverse Chain-of-Thought Generation

author.name: Guangyue Peng, Zongchao Chen, Wen Luo, Yuntao Wen, Wei Li, Ruixiang Feng, Ran Le, Chen Yang, Zhenwei An, Yang Song, Tao Zhang, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes post-hoc rationalization in Reverse Chain-of-Thought generation through a three-level measurement hierarchy (lexical, entropic, probabilistic anchoring). Shows that semantic suppression paradoxically increases deeper forms of anchoring.

entry.title: Low-Pass Filtering Improves Behavioral Alignment of Vision Models

author.name: Max Wolff, Thomas Klein, Evgenia Rusak, Felix Wichmann, Wieland Brendel

entry.summary: Shows that the increased behavioral alignment of generative classifiers with human vision can be largely explained by a low-pass filtering effect from image resizing, challenging previous claims about generative vs discriminative model differences.

entry.title: Will reward-seekers respond to distant incentives?

author.name: Alex Mallen

entry.summary: Analyzes whether reward-seeking AI agents might respond to distant incentives (e.g., future retroactive reinforcement from external actors), arguing this could make even well-trained agents behave like schemers by responding to incentives developers can't control.

entry.title: VeRA: Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation at Scale

author.name: Zerui Cheng, Jiashuo Liu, Chunjie Wu, Jianzhu Yao, Pramod Viswanath, Ge Zhang, Wenhao Huang

entry.summary: VeRA converts benchmark problems into executable specifications with templates, generators, and verifiers to create unlimited novel instances from seed problems, combating benchmark contamination and saturation in LLM evaluation.

entry.title: General learned delegation by clones

author.name: Darren Li, Meiqi Chen, Chenze Shao, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: SELFCEST trains a model via agentic RL to spawn same-weight clones in parallel contexts, learning to allocate generation and context budget across branches. Improves accuracy-cost Pareto frontier on math reasoning and multi-hop QA.

entry.title: Process-Supervised Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Reliable Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Chaeeun Lee, T. Michael Yates, Pasquale Minervini, T. Ian Simpson

entry.summary: Introduces an agent-as-tool reinforcement learning framework for clinical gene-disease validity curation, combining process-level supervision with hierarchical multi-agent coordination. Ensures reasoning follows valid clinical pathways rather than just optimizing outcome accuracy.

entry.title: Competition for attention predicts good-to-bad tipping in AI

author.name: Neil F. Johnson, Frank Y. Huo

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical formula for predicting tipping points in edge AI conversations where models shift from helpful to harmful outputs, based on dot-product competition for attention between context and competing output basins.

entry.title: Training-Induced Bias Toward LLM-Generated Content in Dense Retrieval

author.name: William Xion, Wolfgang Nejdl

entry.summary: Studies training-induced bias in dense retrieval systems toward LLM-generated content, conducting controlled evaluation across training stages and data sources. Challenges the perplexity hypothesis for source bias.

entry.title: IDPruner: Harmonizing Importance and Diversity in Visual Token Pruning for MLLMs

author.name: Yifan Tan, Yifu Sun, Shirui Huang, Hong Liu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Yangdong Deng

entry.summary: Proposes IDPruner, a principled framework for visual token pruning in multimodal LLMs that systematically balances token importance and semantic diversity. Addresses the computational bottleneck of massive visual token volumes in MLLMs.

entry.title: MedScope: Incentivizing "Think with Videos" for Clinical Reasoning via Coarse-to-Fine Tool Calling

author.name: Wenjie Li, Yujie Zhang, Haoran Sun, Xingqi He, Hongcheng Gao, Chenglong Ma, Ming Hu, Guankun Wang, Shiyi Yao, Renhao Yang, Hongliang Ren, Lei Wang, Junjun He, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes MedScope, a tool-using clinical video reasoning model that performs coarse-to-fine evidence seeking over long-form surgical procedures. Interleaves reasoning with targeted tool calls for more accurate and verifiable clinical predictions.

entry.title: MAS-on-the-Fly: Dynamic Adaptation of LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems at Test Time

author.name: Guangyi Liu, Haojun Lin, Huan Zeng, Heng Wang, Quanming Yao

entry.summary: Introduces MASFly, a multi-agent framework enabling dynamic adaptation at test time through retrieval-augmented SOP instantiation and experience-guided supervision with a Watcher agent.

entry.title: Eureka-Audio: Triggering Audio Intelligence in Compact Language Models

author.name: Dan Zhang, Yishu Lei, Jing Hu, Shuwei He, Songhe Deng, Xianlong Luo, Danxiang Zhu, Shikun Feng, Rui Liu, Jingzhou He, Yu Sun, Hua Wu, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: Presents Eureka-Audio, a 1.7B parameter audio language model achieving competitive performance against models 4-18x larger across ASR, audio understanding, and captioning tasks using MoE adapters and end-to-end architecture.

entry.title: A Deployment-Friendly Foundational Framework for Efficient Computational Pathology

author.name: Yu Cai, Cheng Jin, Jiabo Ma, Fengtao Zhou, Yingxue Xu, Zhengrui Guo, Yihui Wang, Zhengyu Zhang, Ling Liang, Yonghao Tan, Pingcheng Dong, Du Cai, On Ki Tang, Chenglong Zhao, Xi Wang, Can Yang, Yali Xu, Jing Cui, Zhenhui Li, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Yueping Liu, Feng Gao, Xiuming Zhang, Li Liang, Hao Chen, Kwang-Ting Cheng

entry.summary: Presents LitePath, a deployment-friendly pathology foundation model framework that distills three large pathology models into a compact model (28x parameter reduction, 403.5x FLOP reduction) with adaptive patch selection for whole slide images.

entry.title: UniWeTok: An Unified Binary Tokenizer with Codebook Size $\mathit{2^{128}}$ for Unified Multimodal Large Language Model

author.name: Shaobin Zhuang, Yuang Ai, Jiaming Han, Weijia Mao, Xiaohui Li, Fangyikang Wang, Xiao Wang, Yan Li, Shanchuan Lin, Kun Xu, Zhenheng Yang, Huaibo Huang, Xiangyu Yue, Hao Chen, Yali Wang

entry.summary: Introduces UniWeTok, a unified binary tokenizer with codebook size 2^128 for multimodal LLMs, using Pre-Post Distillation and Generative-Aware Prior with a convolution-attention hybrid architecture.

entry.title: KernelBlaster: Continual Cross-Task CUDA Optimization via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kris Shengjun Dong, Sahil Modi, Dima Nikiforov, Sana Damani, Edward Lin, Siva Kumar Sastry Hari, Christos Kozyrakis

entry.summary: Proposes KernelBlaster, a Memory-Augmented In-context RL framework for CUDA optimization that enables LLM agents to learn from experience across GPU architectures, aggregating knowledge from prior exploration.

entry.title: Silent Inconsistency in Data-Parallel Full Fine-Tuning: Diagnosing Worker-Level Optimization Misalignment

author.name: Hong Li, Zhen Zhou, Honggang Zhang, Yuping Luo, Xinyue Wang, Han Gong, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: Identifies 'silent inconsistency' in data-parallel LLM training where worker-level optimization dynamics diverge despite synchronized parameters. Proposes a diagnostic framework to detect this using existing training signals and introduces corrective interventions.

entry.title: Exposing Diversity Bias in Deep Generative Models: Statistical Origins and Correction of Diversity Error

author.name: Farzan Farnia, Mohammad Jalali, Azim Ospanov

entry.summary: Demonstrates that deep generative models systematically under-represent diversity compared to real data distributions, using reference-free entropy-based diversity scores (Vendi, RKE). Proposes statistical corrections for this diversity bias.

entry.title: Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training

author.name: Jonathan Lys, Vincent Gripon, Bastien Pasdeloup, Lukas Mauch, Fabien Cardinaux, Ghouthi Boukli Hacene

entry.summary: Proposes inference-time inner looping in pretrained transformers, repeating certain transformer blocks to refine representations without additional training, unlocking latent capabilities already present in the model.

entry.title: A Geometric Analysis of Small-sized Language Model Hallucinations

author.name: Emanuele Ricco, Elia Onofri, Lorenzo Cima, Stefano Cresci, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: Investigates hallucinations in small LLMs through a geometric lens, proving that genuine responses cluster more tightly in embedding space than hallucinated ones. Proposes a label-efficient method achieving >90% F1 from just 30-50 annotations.

entry.title: The Well-Tempered Classifier: Some Elementary Properties of Temperature Scaling

author.name: Pierre-Alexandre Mattei, Bruno Loureiro

entry.summary: Provides rigorous theoretical analysis of temperature scaling for classifiers and LLMs. Shows increasing temperature increases uncertainty for classifiers but challenges the claim that it always increases diversity in LLMs.

entry.title: Text Has Curvature

author.name: Karish Grover, Hanqing Zeng, Yinglong Xia, Christos Faloutsos, Geoffrey J. Gordon

entry.summary: Argues that text has intrinsic curvature, proposes Texture as a word-level discrete curvature signal, and provides theoretical and empirical evidence that semantic inference in natural language is non-flat. Shows curvature can improve downstream tasks.

entry.title: Benchmark Leakage Trap: Can We Trust LLM-based Recommendation?

author.name: Mingqiao Zhang, Qiyao Peng, Yumeng Wang, Chunyuan Liu, Hongtao Liu

entry.summary: Identifies and investigates benchmark data leakage in LLM-based recommendation systems, where LLMs memorize benchmark datasets during pretraining leading to inflated performance. Proposes temporal splitting and decontamination strategies.

entry.title: QuRL: Efficient Reinforcement Learning with Quantized Rollout

author.name: Yuhang Li, Reena Elangovan, Xin Dong, Priyadarshini Panda, Brucek Khailany

entry.summary: Proposes QuRL, which uses quantized actors for faster rollout in RL training of LLMs. Introduces Adaptive Clipping Range to prevent training collapse and addresses weight update lag from quantization.

entry.title: Use What You Know: Causal Foundation Models with Partial Graphs

author.name: Arik Reuter, Anish Dhir, Cristiana Diaconu, Jake Robertson, Ole Ossen, Frank Hutter, Adrian Weller, Mark van der Wilk, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: Introduces methods to condition Causal Foundation Models on partial causal information (full graphs, ancestral info, or partial knowledge), improving predictions over unconditioned CFMs. Co-authored by Bernhard Schölkopf.

entry.title: SpargeAttention2: Trainable Sparse Attention via Hybrid Top-k+Top-p Masking and Distillation Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jintao Zhang, Kai Jiang, Chendong Xiang, Weiqi Feng, Yuezhou Hu, Haocheng Xi, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes SpargeAttention2, a trainable sparse attention method for diffusion models using hybrid Top-k+Top-p masking and distillation fine-tuning. Achieves higher sparsity than training-free methods without degrading generation quality.

entry.title: MC$^2$Mark: Distortion-Free Multi-Bit Watermarking for Long Messages

author.name: Xuehao Cui, Ruibo Chen, Yihan Wu, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Proposes MC²Mark, a distortion-free multi-bit watermarking framework for LLMs that can embed and decode long messages using multi-channel colored reweighting while keeping token distributions unbiased.

entry.title: Open Rubric System: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with Pairwise Adaptive Rubric

author.name: Ruipeng Jia, Yunyi Yang, Yuxin Wu, Yongbo Gai, Siyuan Tao, Mengyu Zhou, Jianhe Lin, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Open Rubric System (OpenRS) for LLM alignment using Pairwise Adaptive Meta-Rubrics and Pointwise Verifiable Rubrics, arguing that reward should be an explicit reasoning process rather than a learned scalar function. Addresses reward hacking in open-ended alignment.

entry.title: MCPShield: A Security Cognition Layer for Adaptive Trust Calibration in Model Context Protocol Agents

author.name: Zhenhong Zhou, Yuanhe Zhang, Hongwei Cai, Moayad Aloqaily, Ouns Bouachir, Linsey Pang, Prakhar Mehrotra, Kun Wang, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: Proposes MCPShield, a security cognition layer for MCP-based LLM agents that provides adaptive trust calibration for third-party tool servers, inspired by human experience-driven tool validation.

entry.title: Fusing Pixels and Genes: Spatially-Aware Learning in Computational Pathology

author.name: Minghao Han, Dingkang Yang, Linhao Qu, Zizhi Chen, Gang Li, Han Wang, Jiacong Wang, Lihua Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes STAMP, integrating spatially-resolved gene expression with pathology images for representation learning. Shows that self-supervised gene-guided training provides robust task-agnostic pathology representations.

entry.title: Flow4R: Unifying 4D Reconstruction and Tracking with Scene Flow

author.name: Shenhan Qian, Ganlin Zhang, Shangzhe Wu, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Proposes Flow4R, a unified framework treating camera-space scene flow as the central representation linking 3D structure, object motion, and camera motion for dynamic scene reconstruction and tracking from two-view inputs.

entry.title: EditCtrl: Disentangled Local and Global Control for Real-Time Generative Video Editing

author.name: Yehonathan Litman, Shikun Liu, Dario Seyb, Nicholas Milef, Yang Zhou, Carl Marshall, Shubham Tulsiani, Caleb Leak

entry.summary: EditCtrl is a video inpainting framework that focuses computation only on masked regions rather than processing the full video context. It uses a local video context module operating on masked tokens with cost proportional to edit size, guided by a lightweight global temporal embedder.

entry.title: Predicting fixed-sample test decisions enables anytime-valid inference

author.name: Chris Holmes, Stephen Walker

entry.summary: Introduces a simple procedure that transforms any fixed-sample hypothesis test into an anytime-valid test while maintaining Type-I error control and near-optimal power, by predicting rejection probability treating future observations as missing data under the null.

entry.title: From Fluent to Verifiable: Claim-Level Auditability for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Razeen A Rasheed, Somnath Banerjee, Animesh Mukherjee, Rima Hazra

entry.summary: Argues that as AI research report generation becomes cheap, claim-level auditability becomes the bottleneck. Proposes auditability as a first-class design target for deep research agents and catalogs failure modes like objective drift and unverifiable inference.

entry.title: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision

author.name: A. Said Gurbuz, Sunghwan Hong, Ahmed Nassar, Marc Pollefeys, Peter Staar

entry.summary: Introduces ScreenParse, a large-scale dataset with dense annotations of all visible UI elements (21M elements across 771K screenshots) for complete screen parsing, enabling better computer-use agents.

entry.title: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation

author.name: Yuyu Guo, Wenjie Yang, Siyuan Yang, Ziyang Liu, Cheng Chen, Yuan Wei, Yun Hu, Yang Huang, Guoliang Hao, Dongsheng Yuan, Jianming Wang, Xin Chen, Hang Yu, Lei Lei, Peng Di

entry.summary: OpAgent introduces online RL for web navigation agents that learn through direct interaction with unconstrained websites, addressing distributional shift from static offline datasets. Includes hierarchical multi-task fine-tuning.

entry.title: Hippocampus: An Efficient and Scalable Memory Module for Agentic AI

author.name: Yi Li, Lianjie Cao, Faraz Ahmed, Puneet Sharma, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: Hippocampus is an agentic memory system using binary signatures for semantic search and a Dynamic Wavelet Matrix for compression and co-indexing, achieving linear scaling and ultra-fast search in compressed domain.

entry.title: Guided Collaboration in Heterogeneous LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Entropy-Based Understanding Assessment and Experience Retrieval

author.name: Linlin Wang, Tianqing Zhu, Laiqiao Qin, Longxiang Gao, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: Studies heterogeneous multi-agent LLM systems and discovers that strong-weak model collaboration can underperform weak-weak combinations due to cognitive mismatching. Proposes entropy-based understanding assessment and experience retrieval to guide collaboration.

entry.title: AllMem: A Memory-centric Recipe for Efficient Long-context Modeling

author.name: Ziming Wang, Xiang Wang, Kailong Peng, Lang Qin, Juan Gabriel Kostelec, Christos Sourmpis, Axel Laborieux, Qinghai Guo

entry.summary: AllMem combines Sliding Window Attention with non-linear Test-Time Training memory networks for ultra-long context modeling, mitigating catastrophic forgetting while reducing computational overhead compared to full attention.

entry.title: Can a Lightweight Automated AI Pipeline Solve Research-Level Mathematical Problems?

author.name: Lve Meng (University of Science, Technology of China, Zhongguancun Academy), Weilong Zhao (Universit\'e Paris Cit\'e), Yanzhi Zhang (Zhongguancun Academy), Haoxiang Guan (Zhongguancun Academy), Jiyan He (Zhongguancun Academy)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a lightweight automated pipeline using next-gen models (Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2 Pro) with citation-based verification can solve research-grade mathematical problems, evaluated on two novel datasets.

entry.title: Neuromem: A Granular Decomposition of the Streaming Lifecycle in External Memory for LLMs

author.name: Ruicheng Zhang, Xinyi Li, Tianyi Xu, Shuhao Zhang, Xiaofei Liao, Hai Jin

entry.summary: Neuromem benchmarks external memory modules under realistic streaming conditions with interleaved insertion-and-retrieval, decomposing the memory lifecycle into five dimensions. Reveals that static evaluation doesn't predict streaming performance.

entry.title: Plan-MCTS: Plan Exploration for Action Exploitation in Web Navigation

author.name: Weiming Zhang, Jihong Wang, Jiamu Zhou, Qingyao Li, Xinbei Ma, Congmin Zheng, Xingyu Lou, Weiwen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang, Jun Wang, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Plan-MCTS reformulates web navigation by shifting MCTS exploration to a semantic Plan Space, decoupling strategic planning from execution. Creates a Dense Plan Tree for efficient exploration and Abstracted Semantic History for state awareness.

entry.title: ForesightSafety Bench: A Frontier Risk Evaluation and Governance Framework towards Safe AI

author.name: Haibo Tong, Feifei Zhao, Linghao Feng, Ruoyu Wu, Ruolin Chen, Lu Jia, Zhou Zhao, Jindong Li, Tenglong Li, Erliang Lin, Shuai Yang, Enmeng Lu, Yinqian Sun, Qian Zhang, Zizhe Ruan, Zeyang Yue, Ping Wu, Huangrui Li, Chengyi Sun, Yi Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes ForesightSafety Bench, a comprehensive AI safety evaluation framework covering 7 fundamental safety pillars extending to embodied AI, AI4Science, social risks, and catastrophic scenarios. Aims to address limitations of current safety benchmarks.

entry.title: World Models for Policy Refinement in StarCraft II

author.name: Yixin Zhang, Ziyi Wang, Yiming Rong, Haoxi Wang, Jinling Jiang, Shuang Xu, Haoran Wu, Shiyu Zhou, Bo Xu

entry.summary: Proposes StarWM, the first world model for StarCraft II that predicts future observations under partial observability, using structured textual representations and a factorized observation space to guide LLM-based decision-making.

entry.title: Real-World Design and Deployment of an Embedded GenAI-powered 9-1-1 Calltaking Training System: Experiences and Lessons Learned

author.name: Zirong Chen, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: Reports on real-world deployment of a GenAI-powered 911 call-taker training system with Metro Nashville, scaling to 190 operational users. Addresses critical staffing shortages in emergency communications.

entry.title: Boltz is a Strong Baseline for Atom-level Representation Learning

author.name: Hyosoon Jang, Hyunjin Seo, Yunhui Jang, Seonghyun Park, Sungsoo Ahn

entry.summary: Shows that Boltz, a protein co-folding model operating at atom-level granularity, provides surprisingly strong baseline representations for small-molecule property prediction tasks like ADMET.

entry.title: Directional Concentration Uncertainty: A representational approach to uncertainty quantification for generative models

author.name: Souradeep Chattopadhyay, Brendan Kennedy, Sai Munikoti, Soumik Sarkar, Karl Pazdernik

entry.summary: Proposes Directional Concentration Uncertainty (DCU), a statistical framework for uncertainty quantification in generative models using von Mises-Fisher distribution to measure geometric dispersion of embeddings.

entry.title: HiST-VLA: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yiru Wang, Zichong Gu, Yu Gao, Anqing Jiang, Zhigang Sun, Shuo Wang, Yuwen Heng, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Proposes HiST-VLA, a hierarchical spatio-temporal vision-language-action model for autonomous driving that enhances 3D spatial and temporal reasoning with dynamic token sparsification for efficiency. Addresses VLA limitations in safety-critical driving scenarios.

entry.title: Assessing Spear-Phishing Website Generation in Large Language Model Coding Agents

author.name: Tailia Malloy, Tegawende F. Bissyande

entry.summary: Assesses the capability of LLM coding agents to generate spear-phishing websites, examining the security implications of increasingly autonomous programming agents in cybersecurity contexts.

entry.title: Metabolic cost of information processing in Poisson variational autoencoders

author.name: Hadi Vafaii, Jacob L. Yates

entry.summary: Explores metabolic cost of information processing in Poisson variational autoencoders, showing that KL divergence becomes proportional to prior firing rates, creating an emergent metabolic cost that couples coding rate to firing rate.

entry.title: FlowHOI: Flow-based Semantics-Grounded Generation of Hand-Object Interactions for Dexterous Robot Manipulation

author.name: Huajian Zeng, Lingyun Chen, Jiaqi Yang, Yuantai Zhang, Fan Shi, Peidong Liu, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: Proposes FlowHOI, a two-stage flow-matching framework for generating semantically grounded hand-object interaction sequences conditioned on egocentric observations, language instructions, and 3D Gaussian splatting scene reconstructions.

entry.title: Arming Data Agents with Tribal Knowledge

author.name: Shubham Agarwal, Asim Biswal, Sepanta Zeighami, Alvin Cheung, Joseph Gonzalez, Aditya G. Parameswaran

entry.summary: Proposes a system for enhancing NL2SQL agents with 'tribal knowledge' - implicit knowledge about how to correctly use database data that goes beyond simple facts. Addresses misconceptions that NL2SQL agents form about real-world databases.

entry.title: AuTAgent: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Tool-Augmented Audio Reasoning

author.name: Siqian Tong, Xuan Li, Yiwei Wang, Baolong Bi, Yujun Cai, Shenghua Liu, Yuchen He, Chengpeng Hao

entry.summary: Proposes AuTAgent, a reinforcement learning framework for audio reasoning that learns when and which external tools to invoke using a differential reward mechanism, avoiding information overload from naive tool use.

entry.title: Pailitao-VL: Unified Embedding and Reranker for Real-Time Multi-Modal Industrial Search

author.name: Lei Chen, Chen Ju, Xu Chen, Zhicheng Wang, Yuheng Jiao, Hongfeng Zhan, Zhaoyang Li, Shihao Xu, Zhixiang Zhao, Tong Jia, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Presents Pailitao-VL, an industrial multi-modal retrieval system shifting from contrastive learning to ID-recognition for embeddings and using a VLM-based reranker. Deployed at scale in production.

entry.title: MOTIF: Learning Action Motifs for Few-shot Cross-Embodiment Transfer

author.name: Heng Zhi, Wentao Tan, Lei Zhu, Fengling Li, Jingjing Li, Guoli Yang, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces MOTIF for few-shot cross-embodiment transfer that decouples embodiment-agnostic spatiotemporal patterns ('action motifs') from heterogeneous action data using vector quantization with progress-aware alignment.

entry.title: MechPert: Mechanistic Consensus as an Inductive Bias for Unseen Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Marc Boubnovski Martell, Josefa Lia Stoisser, Lawrence Phillips, Aditya Misra, Robert Kitchen, Jesper Ferkinghoff-Borg, Jialin Yu, Philip Torr, Kaspar M\"arten

entry.summary: Introduces MechPert, a framework using multiple LLM agents to generate directed regulatory hypotheses for predicting transcriptional responses to unseen genetic perturbations, aggregated through consensus mechanism.

entry.title: Mean Flow Policy with Instantaneous Velocity Constraint for One-step Action Generation

author.name: Guojian Zhan, Letian Tao, Pengcheng Wang, Yixiao Wang, Yiheng Li, Yuxin Chen, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: Proposes Mean Velocity Policy (MVP) for one-step action generation in RL using mean velocity fields with an instantaneous velocity constraint, achieving fast and expressive policy generation.

entry.title: Pawsterior: Variational Flow Matching for Structured Simulation-Based Inference

author.name: Jorge Carrasco-Pollo, Floor Eijkelboom, Jan-Willem van de Meent

entry.summary: Introduces Pawsterior, a variational flow-matching framework for simulation-based inference that handles structured domains (bounded parameters, hybrid discrete-continuous variables) through endpoint-induced affine geometric confinement.

entry.title: Sufficient Conditions for Stability of Minimum-Norm Interpolating Deep ReLU Networks

author.name: Ouns El Harzli, Yoonsoo Nam, Ilja Kuzborskij, Bernardo Cuenca Grau, Ard A. Louis

entry.summary: Establishes sufficient conditions for algorithmic stability of deep ReLU networks that achieve minimum-norm interpolation (zero training error with smallest L2 norm parameters). Provides theoretical generalization guarantees for overparameterized deep networks.

entry.title: EIDOS: Latent-Space Predictive Learning for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Xinxing Zhou, Qingren Yao, Yiji Zhao, Chenghao Liu, Flora Salim, Xiaojie Yuan, Yanlong Wen, Ming Jin

entry.summary: Introduces EIDOS, a time series foundation model family that shifts pretraining from future value prediction to latent-space predictive learning, encouraging structured temporal representations via causal Transformer.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs in Finance Requires Explicit Bias Consideration

author.name: Yaxuan Kong, Hoyoung Lee, Yoontae Hwang, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Bradford Levy, Dhagash Mehta, Qingsong Wen, Chanyeol Choi, Yongjae Lee, Stefan Zohren

entry.summary: Identifies five recurring biases (look-ahead, survivorship, narrative, objective, cost) in financial LLM evaluation, finding none discussed in more than 28% of 164 reviewed papers from 2023-2025.

entry.title: Does Socialization Emerge in AI Agent Society? A Case Study of Moltbook

author.name: Ming Li, Xirui Li, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: First large-scale systemic diagnosis of Moltbook AI agent society, introducing quantitative diagnostic framework measuring semantic stabilization, lexical turnover, influence persistence, and collective consensus in AI social systems.

entry.title: AXE: An Agentic eXploit Engine for Confirming Zero-Day Vulnerability Reports

author.name: Amirali Sajadi, Tu Nguyen, Kostadin Damevski, Preetha Chatterjee

entry.summary: Introduces AXE, a multi-agent framework for web application exploitation that validates vulnerability reports in a grey-box setting using CWE classification and code location metadata.

entry.title: InnoEval: On Research Idea Evaluation as a Knowledge-Grounded, Multi-Perspective Reasoning Problem

author.name: Shuofei Qiao, Yunxiang Wei, Xuehai Wang, Bin Wu, Boyang Xue, Ningyu Zhang, Hossein A. Rahmani, Yanshan Wang, Qiang Zhang, Keyan Ding, Jeff Z. Pan, Huajun Chen, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: Introduces InnoEval, a framework for evaluating research ideas as a knowledge-grounded multi-perspective reasoning problem, using heterogeneous deep knowledge search and multi-criteria assessment to reduce LLM-as-judge bias.

entry.title: WiSparse: Boosting LLM Inference Efficiency with Weight-Aware Mixed Activation Sparsity

author.name: Lei Chen, Yuan Meng, Xiaoyu Zhan, Zhi Wang, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes WiSparse, a training-free activation sparsity method for LLM inference that considers both activation and weight importance, with non-uniform sparsity ratios across blocks. Identifies that less significant activations may align with important weights.

entry.title: Socially-Weighted Alignment: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Furkan Mumcu, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: Proposes Socially-Weighted Alignment (SWA), a game-theoretic framework for multi-agent LLM systems that balances individual agent objectives with group welfare via a social weight parameter. Derives a critical threshold for preventing system overload in congestion games.

entry.title: TikArt: Aperture-Guided Observation for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hao Ding, Zhichuan Yang, Weijie Ge, Ziqin Gao, Chaoyi Lu, Lei Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces TikArt, an aperture-guided agent for fine-grained visual reasoning in MLLMs that uses a Think-Aperture-Observe loop with Zoom and Segment actions to focus on relevant image regions, converting visual cues to linguistic memory.

entry.title: Fluid-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shishir Sharma, Doina Precup, Theodore J. Perkins

entry.summary: Proposes fluid-agent environments where agents can create other agents during MARL training, presents game-theoretic solution concepts, and evaluates several MARL algorithms on fluid variants of standard benchmarks.

entry.title: Scale redundancy and soft gauge fixing in positively homogeneous neural networks

author.name: Rodrigo Carmo Terin

entry.summary: Interprets the scale redundancy in positively homogeneous neural networks as a gauge symmetry from physics, introduces gauge-adapted coordinates, and proposes a soft orbit-selection penalty that stabilizes training by suppressing scale drift.

entry.title: CT-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Lesion Understanding in Computed Tomography

author.name: Qingqing Zhu, Qiao Jin, Tejas S. Mathai, Yin Fang, Zhizheng Wang, Yifan Yang, Maame Sarfo-Gyamfi, Benjamin Hou, Ran Gu, Praveen T. S. Balamuralikrishna, Kenneth C. Wang, Ronald M. Summers, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: Introduces CT-Bench, a benchmark with 20,335 lesions from 7,795 CT studies for evaluating multimodal models on lesion understanding, including localization, description, size estimation, and attribute categorization with 2,850 QA pairs.

entry.title: AnchorWeave: World-Consistent Video Generation with Retrieved Local Spatial Memories

author.name: Zun Wang, Han Lin, Jaehong Yoon, Jaemin Cho, Yue Zhang, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Introduces AnchorWeave, a memory-augmented video generation framework that maintains spatial consistency over long horizons by using local spatial memories and retrieval-based conditioning rather than globally reconstructed 3D scenes.

entry.title: Cold-Start Personalization via Training-Free Priors from Structured World Models

author.name: Avinandan Bose, Shuyue Stella Li, Faeze Brahman, Pang Wei Koh, Simon Shaolei Du, Yulia Tsvetkov, Maryam Fazel, Lin Xiao, Asli Celikyilmaz

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free approach to cold-start personalization by decomposing preference elicitation into offline structure discovery using world models and online questioning, addressing the routing problem of identifying which preference dimensions matter for each user.

entry.title: Optimal Regret for Policy Optimization in Contextual Bandits

author.name: Orin Levy, Yishay Mansour

entry.summary: Presents the first high-probability optimal regret bound for policy optimization in stochastic contextual multi-armed bandits with general offline function approximation. Achieves O(sqrt(K|A|log|F|)) regret.

entry.title: Position Encoding with Random Float Sampling Enhances Length Generalization of Transformers

author.name: Atsushi Shimizu, Shohei Taniguchi, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Introduces Random Float Sampling (RFS), a position encoding strategy using randomly sampled continuous values instead of discrete indices, improving length generalization in transformers. Compatible with existing PE schemes.

entry.title: MAGE: All-[MASK] Block Already Knows Where to Look in Diffusion LLM

author.name: Omin Kwon, Yeonjae Kim, Doyeon Kim, Minseo Kim, Yeonhong Park, Jae W. Lee

entry.summary: Proposes MAGE for block diffusion LLMs, discovering that attention at the first all-[MASK] denoising step reliably predicts important KV entries, enabling a single exact attention pass per block for training-free sparse denoising.

entry.title: Radial-VCReg: More Informative Representation Learning Through Radial Gaussianization

author.name: Yilun Kuang, Yash Dagade, Deep Chakraborty, Erik Learned-Miller, Randall Balestriero, Tim G. J. Rudner, Yann LeCun

entry.summary: Proposes Radial-VCReg, augmenting VCReg self-supervised learning with a radial Gaussianization loss that aligns feature norms with the Chi distribution. Proves this transforms a broader class of distributions towards normality. Co-authored by Yann LeCun.

entry.title: Learning State-Tracking from Code Using Linear RNNs

author.name: Julien Siems, Riccardo Grazzi, Kirill Kalinin, Hitesh Ballani, Babak Rahmani

entry.summary: Shows that linear RNNs capable of state-tracking succeed at code-based permutation composition tasks while Transformers fail, even in next-token prediction setting. Investigates why tracking state in code is difficult for Transformers.

entry.title: LiveNewsBench: Evaluating LLM Web Search Capabilities with Freshly Curated News

author.name: Yunfan Zhang, Kathleen McKeown, Smaranda Muresan

entry.summary: Introduces LiveNewsBench, a continuously updated benchmark for evaluating LLM web search capabilities using fresh news articles that require multi-hop search and reasoning. Ensures separation between internal knowledge and search ability.

entry.title: Why Self-Training Helps and Hurts: Denoising vs. Signal Forgetting

author.name: Mingqi Wu, Archer Y. Yang, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Analyzes iterative self-training in overparameterized linear regression, deriving deterministic-equivalent recursions that separate two forces: signal forgetting (growing) and denoising (decaying), identifying an optimal early stopping point.

entry.title: GTS: Inference-Time Scaling of Latent Reasoning with a Learnable Gaussian Thought Sampler

author.name: Minghan Wang, Ye Bai, Thuy-Trang Vu, Ehsan Shareghi, Gholamreza Haffari

entry.summary: Proposes Gaussian Thought Sampler (GTS) for structured inference-time scaling in latent reasoning models, replacing heuristic perturbations with learnable context-dependent distributions for exploring reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: BPP: Long-Context Robot Imitation Learning by Focusing on Key History Frames

author.name: Max Sobol Mark, Jacky Liang, Maria Attarian, Chuyuan Fu, Debidatta Dwibedi, Dhruv Shah, Aviral Kumar

entry.summary: Addresses the problem of robot policies failing when conditioned on history due to spurious correlations, proposing BPP which identifies and focuses on key history frames. The paper analyzes why policies latch onto incidental features and shows this stems from limited coverage over possible histories during training.

entry.title: Beyond Words: Evaluating and Bridging Epistemic Divergence in User-Agent Interaction via Theory of Mind

author.name: Minyuan Ruan, Ziyue Wang, Kaiming Liu, Yunghwei Lai, Peng Li, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating epistemic divergence between users and LLM agents using Theory of Mind, formalizing ToM as a mechanism for detecting and resolving mismatches between user beliefs and environment states. Creates a benchmark for assessing this capability.

entry.title: PrivAct: Internalizing Contextual Privacy Preservation via Multi-Agent Preference Training

author.name: Yuhan Cheng, Hancheng Ye, Hai Helen Li, Jingwei Sun, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: Proposes PrivAct, a multi-agent learning framework that internalizes contextual privacy preservation into LLM agent behavior through preference training, rather than relying on brittle external inference-time interventions.

entry.title: Beyond Token-Level Policy Gradients for Complex Reasoning with Large Language Models

author.name: Mufan Xu, Kehai Chen, Xuefeng Bai, Zhengyu Niu, Muyun Yang, Tiejun Zhao, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-token Policy Gradient Optimization (MPO) that treats sequences of K consecutive tokens as unified semantic actions for policy gradient training, addressing the mismatch between token-level optimization and block-level reasoning.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of LLMs in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xin Qiu, Junlong Tong, Yirong Sun, Yunpu Ma, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale study of LLM-based time series forecasting across 8 billion observations and 17 scenarios, demonstrating that LLMs do improve forecasting performance, especially in cross-domain generalization, contradicting prior claims of no benefit.

entry.title: Embed-RL: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning-Driven Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Haonan Jiang, Yuji Wang, Yongjie Zhu, Xin Lu, Wenyu Qin, Meng Wang, Pengfei Wan, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes Embed-RL, using reinforcement learning to train a Reasoner that produces evidential traceability Chain-of-Thought for universal multimodal embeddings. Bridges generative reasoning and discriminative retrieval.

entry.title: EgoSound: Benchmarking Sound Understanding in Egocentric Videos

author.name: Bingwen Zhu, Yuqian Fu, Qiaole Dong, Guolei Sun, Tianwen Qian, Yuzheng Wu, Danda Pani Paudel, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: Introduces EgoSound, the first benchmark for evaluating egocentric sound understanding in multimodal LLMs, with a seven-task taxonomy spanning sound perception, spatial reasoning, and causal interaction.

entry.title: MedVAR: Towards Scalable and Efficient Medical Image Generation via Next-scale Autoregressive Prediction

author.name: Zhicheng He, Yunpeng Zhao, Junde Wu, Ziwei Niu, Zijun Li, Lanfen Lin, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: Introduces MedVAR, the first autoregressive foundation model for medical image synthesis using next-scale prediction, generating images coarse-to-fine with multi-scale representations useful for downstream tasks.

entry.title: YOLO26: A Comprehensive Architecture Overview and Key Improvements
